title: Infection Spread Simulation V — Optimal Initial Burn
prompt:
This standalone problem is the fifth exercise in the Infection Spread Simulation series. Use `HEALTHY = 0`, `INFECTED = 1`, `IMMUNE = 2`, and `BURNED = 4`.

Implement `best_initial_burn(grid, simulate)`. Before the first simulated day, burn exactly one complete row or one complete column by replacing its cells with `BURNED`. The provided callback `simulate(candidate_grid)` implements Part IV and returns `(stable_days, dead_count, final_grid)`. Evaluate every possible row and column action.

Choose the action that minimizes `(dead_count, stable_days)`. Break remaining ties by preferring rows over columns, then the lower index. Return `(dead_count, stable_days, axis, index, final_grid)`, where `axis` is `"row"` or `"col"`. You may assume the grid is non-empty and rectangular, every cell is `HEALTHY`, `INFECTED`, or `IMMUNE`, and the callback follows its contract; you do not need to validate these inputs. Neither the input grid nor a previously evaluated candidate may be mutated. You do not need to reimplement Parts I–IV.
